result.title: SpatialCast: Reading the 3D World via Cast Shadows
result.comment: 10 pages (main paper), 7 pages (supplementary material), 5 figures and 6 tables in the main paper
result.summary: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) advance toward understanding and interacting with the physical world, spatial reasoning becomes essential for understanding scene structure and anticipating the effects of physical changes. Existing spatial benchmarks have made substantial progress in evaluating spatial relations, memory, and viewpoint reasoning, but less systematically assess how models connect physical scene conditions with visual observations. We introduce SpatialCast, a benchmark that uses cast shadows to evaluate this ability. Cast shadows provide observable evidence of a 3D scene. Their image appearance depends on object geometry and pose, illumination, and viewpoint. We examine this relationship through three complementary tasks that assess scene-projection consistency, predict intervention-induced changes, and infer the physical changes behind visual transitions. The benchmark contains 21,000 synthetic questions with separate scene and geometry test partitions, complemented by 200 SpatialCast-Real questions from 20 photographed scenes. Evaluations show that closed-source MLLMs outperform general-purpose open-weight MLLMs and MLLMs designed for spatial reasoning, which remain near chance on the synthetic benchmark, while even strong closed-source models struggle with shadow-length and light-height judgments. We also use SpatialCast training data for GRPO post-training, improving open-weight MLLM performance on the benchmark. Further evaluations show improvements on several external spatial benchmarks, suggesting transfer of the learned capabilities. These experiments support SpatialCast as a controlled resource for diagnosing spatial reasoning capabilities and studying their learning and generalization.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SpatialCast 基准，利用投影阴影考察 MLLM 能否把 3D 场景的几何、位姿、光照与视角同图像观察联系起来，并设置三类任务评估投影一致性、干预后的变化预测及由视觉变化反推物理变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 它直接诊断多模态模型能否筛选并利用视觉证据推断场景结构与物理变化，与 LVR 中的视觉信息保留、证据筛选和因果作用评估有明确联系，值得关注其任务设计与失败模式。
